C-ASM-001E.title_zh: 制针厂：分工的第一台发动机
C-ASM-001E.description_zh: 《国富论》开篇场景（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-001E.title_en: The Pin Factory: Division of Labour as the First Engine of Wealth
C-ASM-001E.description_en: The opening scene of The Wealth of Nations (1776): one untrained workman performing all eighteen operations alone 'could scarce make one pin in a day, certainly not twenty'; but ten workers split among drawing, cutting, pointing, and heading 'upward of forty-eight thousand pins in a day.' Productivity is a function of structure, not the sum of diligence—division of labour is wealth's first engine, and its extent is limited by the size of the market.

C-ASM-002E.title_zh: 屠夫、酿酒师与面包师：看不见的手
C-ASM-002E.description_zh: 《国富论》第一篇第二章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-002E.title_en: The Butcher, the Brewer, and the Baker: The Invisible Hand
C-ASM-002E.description_en: Book I, ch.2 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest. We address ourselves not to their humanity but to their self-love.' Cooperation among strangers is rewritten from benevolence into mechanism: address self-love, let prices carry information—and the individual, 'led by an invisible hand,' promotes an end no part of his intention, provided the institutions of natural liberty stand.

C-ASM-003E.title_zh: 公正旁观者：心中的那个人
C-ASM-003E.description_zh: 《道德情操论》第三篇（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-003E.title_en: The Impartial Spectator: The Man Within
C-ASM-003E.description_en: Part III of The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759): 'When I endeavour to examine my own conduct, I divide myself into two persons—the examiner and judge, and the person whose conduct is examined.' Moral judgment runs on imaginative position-taking (sympathy) and matures by upgrading the partial spectator of one's circle into the abstract impartial one; yet the man within can be corrupted by admiring the rich and neglecting the poor—Smith's late-life addition of a whole chapter on that corruption.

C-ASM-004E.title_zh: 灯塔与收费公路：公共品的判据
C-ASM-004E.description_zh: 《国富论》第五篇（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-004E.title_en: Lighthouses and Toll Roads: The Test for Public Goods
C-ASM-004E.description_en: Book V of The Wealth of Nations (1776): the sovereign's duty covers works 'which could never repay the expense to any individual or small number of individuals'—lighthouses, roads, bridges, education—while toll roads and bridge dues should be recovered from those who use them. The boundary of the state is not a philosophical stance but a cost-recovery test, and even communalized works stay under efficiency audit; Coase's 1974 study of Britain's private lighthouses later sharpened the Smithian lesson to check institutional facts first.

C-ASM-005E.title_zh: 中华帝国与小指：思想实验的极限
C-ASM-005E.description_zh: 《道德情操论》第三篇第三章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-005E.title_en: The Earthquake in China and the Little Finger: The Limits of Sympathy
C-ASM-005E.description_en: Part III, ch.3 of The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759): 'Let us suppose the empire of China was suddenly swallowed by an earthquake; the man of humanity in Europe, who heard of it, would express much sorrow and pursue his business or pleasure as usual—yet if he were to lose his little finger tomorrow, he would not sleep tonight.' An extreme hypothetical strips the noise of custom and rhetoric, baring the real structure of moral intuition: action follows the tension between spectating one's own situation and imagining another's.

C-ASM-006E.title_zh: 富人之源：节俭而非挥霍
C-ASM-006E.description_zh: 《国富论》第二篇第三章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-006E.title_en: The Source of the Wealthy: Frugality, Not Profusion
C-ASM-006E.description_en: Book II, ch.3 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'Capitals are increased by the private frugality and good conduct of individuals, silently and gradually accumulated. It is this, not the profusion of government, which has brought nations from poverty to opulence.' The politician who would direct private capital assumes 'an authority which could safely be trusted to no council or senate whatever'; every prodigal act is a deduction from the public capital, and every frugal man a public benefactor.

C-ASM-007E.title_zh: 同业密谋：对游说的最早预警
C-ASM-007E.description_zh: 《国富论》第一篇第十章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-007E.title_en: The Conspiracy of the Same Trade: The First Warning against Lobbying
C-ASM-007E.description_en: Book I, ch.10 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'People of the same trade seldom meet together, even for merriment and diversion, but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices.' Collusion is structural, not a moral defect, so the answer must be institutional; 'the proposal of any new law or regulation of commerce which comes from this order ought always to be listened to with great precaution, and never adopted till after long and careful examination'—the ancestor of antitrust and anti-lobbying discourse, to be read in both directions (masters' tacit combination to keep wages down included).

C-ASM-008E.title_zh: 水与钻石：价值悖论的双层拆分
C-ASM-008E.description_zh: 《国富论》第一篇第四章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-008E.title_en: Water and Diamond: Splitting the Value Paradox
C-ASM-008E.description_en: Book I, ch.4 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'The word value has two different meanings—value in use, and value in exchange. Water has the greatest value in use and scarce any in exchange; a diamond has scarce any value in use, and a great quantity of other goods may frequently be had in exchange for it.' Splitting the senses dissolves the ancient paradox, and Smith's first answer—'labour is the real measure of the exchangeable value of all commodities'—hands off unfinished business that Ricardo, the marginalists, and Marx each took up in turn.

C-ASM-009E.title_zh: 税收四则：量能、确定、便利、经济
C-ASM-009E.description_zh: 《国富论》第五篇第二编（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-009E.description_en: Book V of The Wealth of Nations (1776): the subjects should contribute 'in proportion to their respective abilities' (equality); 'the tax which each individual is bound to pay ought to be certain and not arbitrary' (certainty); payment 'ought to be convenient' (convenience); and every tax 'ought to be so contrived as to take out of the pockets of the people as little as possible over and above what it brings into the public treasury' (economy). Smith runs the four maxims against Britain's poll taxes and tithes—their regressivity and arbitrariness named point by point—and a tax 'not in itself very grievous' becomes oppressive 'by a very small degree of uncertainty.'

C-ASM-010E.title_zh: 自然自由体系：主权者只剩三件事
C-ASM-010E.description_zh: 《国富论》第四篇第九章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-010E.title_en: The System of Natural Liberty: Three Duties of the Sovereign
C-ASM-010E.description_en: Book IV, ch.9 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'All systems either of preference or of restraint being completely taken away, the obvious and simple system of natural liberty establishes itself of its own accord. Every man, so long as he does not violate the laws of justice, is left perfectly free to pursue his own interest his own way.' The sovereign is discharged from superintending private industry—its duty 'only of three kinds: defence, justice, and certain public works.' 'Peace, easy taxes, and a tolerable administration of justice' is the best recipe for national opulence; his proposed non-monopolizing empire appeared the same year as the Declaration of Independence.
